rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose term for a product, project, or book launch event.

example.english: The launch for this new book is next week.
example.traditional: 呢本新書嘅發布會下星期舉行。
example.jyutping: ni1 bun2 san1 syu1 ge3 faat3 bou3 wui2 haa6 sing1 kei4 geoi2 hang4

rows.note: Use this specifically for a ceremony marking the launch of a ship or vessel.

example.english: The launch ceremony for this ship will be held on Saturday.
example.traditional: 呢艘船嘅下水禮星期六舉行。
example.jyutping: ni1 sau1 syun4 ge3 haa6 seoi2 lai5 sing1 kei4 luk6 geoi2 hang4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice for starting an app or program.

example.english: I can launch the program with one tap.
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 gam6 zau6 hoi1 dou2 go3 cing4 sik1

rows.note: Use this for putting a product or a new project out for people to use, buy, or participate in.

example.english: The company will launch a new phone next month.
example.traditional: 間公司下個月會推出新款手機。
example.jyutping: gaan1 gung1 si1 haa6 go3 jyut6 wui5 teoi1 ceot1 san1 fun2 sau2 gei1

rows.note: Use this for beginning and carrying out a project or course of action, rather than merely announcing it.

example.english: We will formally launch this project tomorrow.
example.traditional: 我哋聽日正式開展呢個計劃。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 zing3 sik1 hoi1 zin2 ni1 go3 gai3 waak6

rows.note: Use this for sending a rocket or other projectile upward into flight.

example.english: The rocket will launch into the sky as soon as the countdown ends.
example.traditional: 支火箭倒數完就射上天。
example.jyutping: zi1 fo2 zin3 dou2 sou3 jyun4 zau6 se6 soeng5 tin1
